title: Lifespan development
note: Development runs from conception to old age in three domains: physical, cognitive and psychosocial. Piaget saw children as active thinkers moving through four stages; Erikson described a social challenge at each stage of life. Genes and experience always work together, so 'nature or nurture' is really 'nature and nurture.'

read.title: How children build their minds
text: Jean Piaget watched children closely and concluded that they are not small adults with less knowledge. They think in different ways at different ages, actively building mental frameworks called schemas.

Children grow their schemas in two ways. In assimilation, they fit something new into what they already know, as when a toddler calls a sheep a 'dog.' In accommodation, they change the schema when it fails, learning that sheep and dogs are different animals.

Piaget described four stages. In the sensorimotor stage, infants learn through their senses and actions and come to understand object permanence: a toy hidden under a blanket still exists. In the preoperational stage, children use words and pretend play but are egocentric, struggling to see another person's point of view. In the concrete operational stage, they reason logically about real objects and master conservation, knowing that water poured into a taller glass is the same amount. In the formal operational stage, adolescents can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

Later research refined the picture. Children often reach milestones earlier than Piaget thought, and development may be more gradual than strict stages suggest. Lev Vygotsky added that learning is social: children develop language and thought through interaction with the people and culture around them.
